hero.title: TeraGoogle: The Long-Term Web Archive
hero.subtitle: TeraGoogle is Google's petabyte-scale long-term document storage system, the persistent memory of the web. While the serving index (SegIndexer) stores only the most relevant documents for fast retrieval, TeraGoogle maintains the complete historical archive of everything Google has ever crawled. This enables historical data analysis, content change tracking, and recovery of documents removed from the serving index. With perfect 100/100 corroboration across API leak, DOJ evidence, and 20 confirmed patents, TeraGoogle is a Tier 1 infrastructure signal. Its most significant SEO implication: Google remembers everything, including content you've deleted, domain history you've tried to bury, and link patterns that have changed over time.

keyInsight.label: Key Insight from API Leak + DOJ + Patents
keyInsight.text: TeraGoogle achieves 100% corroboration (Tier 1) across three independent sources. The API leak places it in the TeraGoogle module as 'long-term memory storage for secondary indexing.' The DOJ classifies it under Infrastructure/Storage as 'long-term document storage for maintaining the full web archive.' Patent US7346839 (by Anurag Acharya, Matt Cutts, Jeffrey Dean, Paul Haahr, and others) describes using historical data for document scoring, which relies on TeraGoogle's archive. The key implication: Google's ranking system has access to your site's entire history, including past content, historical link profiles, domain ownership changes, and quality trajectory over time.

pillars.title: Patent Evidence (20 Patents)
items: Patent US7346839: Information retrieval based on historical data (Acharya, Cutts, Dean, Haahr, Henzinger, Hoelzle, Lawrence, Pfleger, Sercinoglu, Tong) - 56 claims. System scores documents based on history: content changes, link acquisition rate, domain registration, anchor text evolution. Requires TeraGoogle's archive.
Patent US6285999: Method for node ranking in a linked database - PageRank foundation. Historical link data from TeraGoogle enables tracking link graph evolution.
Patent US7716225: Reasonable Surfer - Link valuation model that benefits from historical click pattern data stored in TeraGoogle.
Patent US7058628: Systems and methods for providing search results - Historical document data used for result quality assessment.
20 patents total, many by Google's founding engineers (Dean, Henzinger, Haahr). These patents consistently reference historical document data that requires persistent storage at web scale.

pillars.title: API Leak: TeraGoogle Signal
items: TeraGoogle (TeraGoogle module): Long-term memory storage mechanism for secondary indexing. Tier 2 match, 100/100 corroboration, 20 matched patents.
Categorized under technical-crawl, placing it in the infrastructure layer alongside Trawler and SegIndexer.
The 'secondary indexing' description confirms TeraGoogle as the backup/archive layer behind SegIndexer's serving index.
20 patent matches indicate TeraGoogle is deeply integrated into Google's document processing and historical analysis systems.

pillars.title: DOJ Trial: Infrastructure Confirmation
items: TeraGoogle (Storage module, Infrastructure system): Confirmed as 'long-term document storage system for maintaining the full web archive.' Cross-reference evidence.
Placed under Infrastructure system in DOJ documentation, alongside Trawler (crawling), SegIndexer (serving index), and other core systems.
The 'full web archive' description confirms TeraGoogle stores everything Google has crawled, not just currently-indexed documents.
Historical document access enables Google to evaluate: domain age, content evolution, link acquisition patterns, penalty history, and ownership changes.

pillars.title: How Historical Data Affects Rankings
items: Google remembers deleted content: Pages you've removed, thin content you've replaced, and spam you've cleaned up are still in TeraGoogle. Historical quality trajectory matters.
Link acquisition rate is tracked: Patent US7346839 explicitly scores based on link velocity. Sudden spikes in backlinks are detectable against historical patterns. Natural growth rewarded.
Domain history persists: Buying an expired domain doesn't erase its history. Previous penalties, spam associations, and quality scores from the old owner are accessible via TeraGoogle.
Content freshness signals need history: The Freshness system compares current content against historical versions stored in TeraGoogle to measure meaningful updates vs. cosmetic changes.
Anchor text evolution tracked: Changes in your backlink anchor text profile over time are visible. Sudden pivot to exact-match anchors is detectable against your historical profile.

Quality trajectory matters: A site consistently improving content quality over years builds a positive historical signal. A site that degraded from high-quality to thin content has a negative trajectory.
Penalty recovery takes time: Even after fixing issues, the historical record of problems persists. Recovery requires sustained quality improvement to override historical negative signals.
400B+ documents archived: TeraGoogle stores the complete archive at petabyte scale. Nothing crawled is ever truly forgotten.

calculations.name: Link Velocity Anomaly Detection
calculations.how: TeraGoogle's historical archive enables comparing current link acquisition rate against the site's historical baseline. Sudden spikes in link velocity (especially from correlated domains) are detectable against the long-term pattern. Steady organic growth scores positively. Unnatural spikes trigger further investigation via SpamBrain/IndyRank.
calculations.formula: LinkVelocity(site, t) = (new_links_month(t) - historical_avg) / historical_stddev // z-score of current link acquisition rate // high positive = unnatural spike (suspicious) // steady around 0 = organic growth (positive) // requires TeraGoogle historical archive
calculations.patents: Patent: US7346839 (56 claims on historical data scoring)
calculations.affects: Affected by: link acquisition rate, historical baseline, source domain correlation. Natural link growth rewarded; sudden spikes flagged.

calculations.name: Historical Data Scoring (US7346839)
calculations.how: Documents are scored based on multiple types of historical data stored in TeraGoogle. The patent identifies several historical factors: when the document was first indexed, how its content has changed over time, how its link profile has evolved, domain registration and renewal patterns, and anchor text changes. The system generates a score that adjusts the document's ranking based on these temporal patterns.
calculations.formula: HistoryScore(doc) = f( first_indexed_date, content_change_rate, link_acquisition_velocity, domain_registration_history, anchor_text_evolution ) // Steady growth > sudden spikes // Consistent quality > volatile quality // Historical data from TeraGoogle archive
calculations.patents: Patent: US7346839 (56 claims, 10 inventors including Cutts, Dean, Haahr)
calculations.affects: Affected by: domain age, content update patterns, link velocity, registration stability, anchor text consistency

calculations.name: Tiered Storage Architecture
calculations.how: Google uses a tiered storage architecture. SegIndexer maintains the actively-served index in three tiers: Base (high-quality), Zeppelins (mid-tier), and Rafts (low-priority). TeraGoogle sits behind all tiers as the persistent archive. Documents can move between tiers based on quality and freshness, but TeraGoogle always retains the historical record.
calculations.formula: Storage = { SegIndexer: { Base: // High-quality, fast serving Zeppelins: // Mid-tier, slower access Rafts: // Low-priority, supplemental }, TeraGoogle: // Complete archive, petabytes // Historical data for all docs // Never deleted, always accessible }
calculations.affects: Affected by: document quality tier, freshness, crawl frequency. TeraGoogle retains documents even when they drop from serving index.

stages.name: Trawler Crawl
stages.detail: Trawler fetches pages from the web. Raw content passed to processing pipeline.

stages.name: Processing & Rendering
stages.detail: Content processed, JavaScript rendered (HtmlrenderWebkit), metadata extracted, quality signals computed.

stages.name: WebMirror Deduplication
stages.detail: Duplicates detected via SimHash. Canonical URLs selected. Non-canonical pages marked.

stages.name: TeraGoogle Archive
stages.detail: ALL processed documents stored in TeraGoogle persistent archive. Historical versions maintained. Nothing is deleted.

stages.name: SegIndexer Tiering
stages.detail: Qualifying documents promoted to serving index tiers (Base/Zeppelins/Rafts). Quality and freshness determine tier placement.

stages.name: Historical Analysis
stages.detail: Ranking systems query TeraGoogle for historical data: content changes, link evolution, domain history. Feeds US7346839 scoring.

timeline.title: Historical Data Patent Filed
timeline.desc: US7346839 filed by Acharya, Cutts, Dean, Haahr et al. 56 claims describing historical document scoring. Requires persistent archive (TeraGoogle).

timeline.title: Historical Data Patent Granted
timeline.desc: US7346839 granted. Google can now officially score documents based on content change patterns, link velocity, and domain history.

timeline.title: Petabyte-Scale Storage
timeline.desc: TeraGoogle scales to petabytes to accommodate the growing web. 400B+ documents archived for historical analysis.

timeline.title: API Leak Confirmation
timeline.desc: TeraGoogle confirmed as 'long-term memory storage mechanism for secondary indexing.' 100/100 corroboration, 20 matched patents.

timeline.title: DOJ Infrastructure Evidence
timeline.desc: DOJ documents confirm TeraGoogle under Infrastructure/Storage as 'long-term document storage system for maintaining the full web archive.'

contradictions.publicClaim: You can request removal of URLs from Google Search. Removed content will no longer appear in search results.
contradictions.internalSource: DOJ + Leak: TeraGoogle retains 'full web archive'
contradictions.internalClaim: URL removal tools remove content from the serving index (SegIndexer) but TeraGoogle retains the historical archive permanently. Patent US7346839 uses historical data for scoring, meaning removed content's history still influences rankings. Google 'remembers everything, including content you've deleted.'

contradictions.publicClaim: Buying a domain that was previously used by someone else is fine. Google evaluates sites based on their current content.
contradictions.internalSource: Patent US7346839: Historical data scoring + TeraGoogle archive
contradictions.internalClaim: Patent US7346839 explicitly scores documents based on domain registration history, content evolution, link acquisition patterns, and historical quality trajectory. TeraGoogle stores the complete history of every domain ever crawled. Previous penalties, spam associations, and quality scores from prior owners remain accessible and can influence current rankings.

contradictions.publicClaim: Updating your content can help it stay relevant. Google looks at the current version of your pages.
contradictions.internalSource: TeraGoogle: Historical content change tracking + US7346839
contradictions.internalClaim: Google compares current content against historical versions stored in TeraGoogle to distinguish meaningful updates from cosmetic changes (date changes, minor rewording). The freshness system uses this delta analysis. Superficial 'updates' that don't materially change content are detectable against the historical record and may not trigger freshness benefits.
